scope: Test `@rx` with a span-only compile, and run the capturing compile only when a rule matches and needs its captures
Keep every `@rx` on zig-regex's linear engine where its semantics allow, instead of the backtracker
Cut per-request bytes on the CRS path: zig-waf allocates 1.1 MiB per clean GET and 3.8 MiB per 973-byte form, against ModSecurity's 0.9 and 1.8 MiB
Record `zig build lab` numbers before and after each change in docs/benchmark-lab.md
out_of_scope: Reaching ModSecurity's latency, which needs P2.21 (P9.39)
Byte-mode and dotall compilation of `@rx` (zig-utils/zig-waf#89 and #90), which this builds on
Moving @pm and phrase matching onto zig-regex literals (P9.09)
notes: Profile in zig-utils/zig-waf#86 at 374f61a: 82% of crs-form-post's time is inside zig-regex's backtracker and under 3% in transformations. Moving every pattern onto the linear engine saved about 18% on CRS's 294 patterns, with the same verdicts
Four rules take 38% of the form's time (934100, 942360, 942190, 941140), and the top 25 take 74%
The lab's first results (zig-utils/zig-waf#6, f6a40a2): zig-waf is the cheapest engine with no rules and loads CRS fastest, so the gap is in rule evaluation
accept: `zig build lab` p50 drops on crs-get, crs-form-post and crs-json-post against 5666abd (every CRS rule compiling, GET 6.78 ms, form 20.40 ms, JSON 95.54 ms p50), on the same machine, with the numbers in docs/benchmark-lab.md
Zero mismatches across every lab scenario, and the FTW and differential suites still pass

scope: A benchmark of every CRS 4.28.0 `@rx` pattern against the zig-waf lab's inputs (its form fields, GET values, headers and five attacks), compiled the way zig-waf compiles them, next to PCRE2 10.47 with and without JIT
Profile the costliest patterns on the linear engine: CRS's large generated keyword alternations (PHP function names, Unix commands) and `(?i)` alternations with lazy quantifiers
Speed up those shapes in the lazy DFA, or with a literal prefilter in front of it, with identical match results
Record before and after numbers with the benchmark
out_of_scope: A JIT that emits machine code
Match and depth limits, and ruleset caches (zig-utils/zig-regex#16)
CRS patterns zig-regex cannot compile yet (zig-utils/zig-waf#89)
notes: Measured in zig-utils/zig-waf#86 on 294 patterns and 23 inputs: zig-regex 0.5.1 takes 41.1 ms as zig-waf compiles today and 33.6 ms span-only in byte mode, against 7.8 ms for PCRE2 without JIT and 0.9 ms with JIT. zig-regex 0.2.1 took 822 ms
benchmarks/pcre2 already has a PCRE2 harness to build the comparison on
CRS is Apache-2.0: vendored patterns carry its license and notice, or the benchmark reads them from a CRS checkout
accept: The CRS benchmark runs with one documented command
zig-regex's total time on it is at or below PCRE2 10.47 without JIT on the same machine
Match results equal PCRE2's for every pattern both engines compile, on every input
`zig build test` and the differential suites pass

goal: The backtracking engine finds every match PCRE2 finds for a lazy loop over a group of lazy quantifiers, so a capturing compile answers the same as a span-only one.
scope: Find why the backtracker gives up on `^(?:[^']*?'[^']*?'[^']*?)*?'` before trying the iteration counts that match
Fix it in the engine, with leftmost-first match spans and captures equal to PCRE2's
Tests for the reductions below and for the CRS 942xxx pattern they come from, each failing on 0.5.2
A differential run of lazy-loop shapes against PCRE2
out_of_scope: ECMAScript-mode disagreements on quantified alternations (zig-utils/zig-regex#30), unless the same cause
notes: Found by the zig-waf session while working zig-utils/zig-waf#87. With bytes, dot_all and multiline, `^(?:[^']*?'[^']*?'[^']*?)*?'` compiled with captures (backtracker) and run with Matcher.find gives no match on `a'b'c'` and `1' or 'a'='a`. PCRE2 10.47 matches [0,6) and [0,9), and compileWithoutCaptures (Thompson engines) matches both. All agree there is no match in `a'b'`
The greedy form `^(?:[^']*'[^']*'[^']*)*'` compiles to the Thompson engine and is right; the lazy form selects the backtracker
zig-waf now tests `@rx` with the span-only compile and captures only on a match, so its block decision is right, but its captured values can be missing
accept: Both reductions and the CRS pattern match where PCRE2 does, with PCRE2's spans, through compileWithFlags and through Matcher.find
A differential run of generated lazy-loop patterns finds no disagreement with PCRE2
`zig build test` passes

goal: Patterns with a backreference get the zig-utils/zig-regex#57 fix too: a loop over a body with choices gives part of an iteration back when what follows needs it, without going exponential.
scope: Make the loop memo valid with backreferences, keying its states on the capture spans the rest of the match reads, or bound the continuation matcher another way for these patterns
Route such patterns' loops to the continuation matcher as the #57 fix routes patterns without a backreference
Tests from the #57 reductions with a backreference added, each failing at zig-regex 9e67b53
out_of_scope: Atomic groups, which also keep the memo off
notes: The #57 fix leaves these patterns on the old matching because, without the memo, the continuation matcher explores such loops exponentially: `(["'])(?:\w+\s?)*\1` on a 26-byte quoted word timed out where the old engine took 174 steps
accept: `(['"])(?:a|ab)*c\1` and similar backreference forms of the #57 reductions match where PCRE2 does
`(["'])(?:\w+\s?)*\1` on a 26-byte quoted identifier stays within a few hundred steps
`zig build test` passes

goal: In PCRE mode the backtracker takes an empty loop iteration as PCRE2 does, so the remaining disagreements in `MODE=regex benchmarks/pcre2/diff.sh` go away.
scope: Outside ECMAScript mode, let the old engine's loops accept an empty iteration and stop there (unbounded) or go on to the next copy (bounded), as the continuation matcher's PCRE-mode pieces already do
Keep ECMAScript mode's RepeatMatcher rule
Rerun the three-seed differential and update docs/BENCHMARKS.md
out_of_scope: Program (Thompson) engines, whose empty-iteration difference docs/BENCHMARKS.md already describes
notes: After #57, 52 disagreements remain over three seeds of 50,000 cases; all start where PCRE2's match starts and are longer, from loops whose body can match empty (`(?:.{0,2}?){1,3}`, `(?s:.*?){2,}`)
Also `(?:(?:a|ab)*?){1,3}` on `abcbc` gives [0,1] where PCRE2 gives [0,0]
accept: `MODE=regex benchmarks/pcre2/diff.sh 50000` on seeds 1 to 3 shows no disagreement from empty iterations
ECMAScript-mode results unchanged against node
`zig build test` passes

goal: The backtracker never reports a miss because an allocation failed: every allocation failure reaches the caller as OutOfMemory.
scope: Replace each `catch return null`, `catch return false`, `catch continue` and `catch return;` on an allocation in the old engine with a path that sets `match_error` (47 sites at 9e67b53)
An allocation-failure sweep test over patterns that reach each path, asserting every result is correct or OutOfMemory
out_of_scope: The continuation matcher, which already reports allocation failures
notes: The engine's own comment on `match_error` says choice traversal must not turn allocation failures into ordinary misses; these sites predate it
accept: An allocation-failure sweep of a loop-heavy pattern on the old engine gives the right answer or OutOfMemory at every failure point
`zig build test` passes

goal: In PCRE mode a group inside a loop keeps the capture an earlier iteration set when a later iteration does not set it, as PCRE2 does.
scope: Stop clearing a loop body's captures at each iteration in the old engine outside ECMAScript mode, for `*`, `+`, `?` and counted repeats
Tests comparing captures with PCRE2 and, in ECMAScript mode, with node
notes: `(?:b|(a)){0,3}` and `(?:b|(a))*` on `ab` give group 1 unset where PCRE2 gives 0:1, in 0.5.2 and at 9e67b53; the #57 fix already keeps them in the pieces it hands to the continuation matcher
accept: `(?:b|(a)){0,3}`, `(?:b|(a))*` and `(?:b|(a))+` on `ab` give group 1 = 0:1 in PCRE mode and unset in ECMAScript mode
`zig build test` passes

goal: In PCRE mode a lookbehind's captures and backreferences behave as PCRE2's, which matches the lookbehind body forwards from its start.
scope: In PCRE mode, match a lookbehind body forwards: find the start the body can begin at, then run the body left to right to the current position, so groups are set before a reference to their right and a loop's last iteration is its rightmost
Keep the right-to-left matching for ECMAScript mode, whose lookbehinds run backwards by the spec
Tests comparing spans and captures with PCRE2 and, in ECMAScript mode, with node
notes: The engine matches every lookbehind right to left, as ECMAScript does, so in PCRE mode a reference to a group on its left sees the group unset and one to a group on its right sees it set

At 95cfb43: `(?<=(a)\1)c` on `aac` finds no match (PCRE2 2:3, group 0:1); `(?<=\1(a))c` on `aac` matches (PCRE2 no match); `(?<=(\w){3})f` on `abcdef` captures `c` (PCRE2 `e`); `(?<=(a)(?<=\1)b)c` on `abc` finds no match (PCRE2 2:3)
Before #62 an unset backreference matched empty in PCRE mode too, which made some of these match by accident (`(?<=(a)\1)c` matched with group 1:2); the #62 comment lists the cases
PCRE2 requires a lookbehind to have a bounded length, so the forward start can be searched over a bounded window
accept: The four patterns in the notes give PCRE2's spans and captures in PCRE mode
ECMAScript-mode output is unchanged over the differential corpus
CRS still matches identically to PCRE2, with no slowdown in the CRS benchmark
`zig build test` passes
